title: Functor categories out of a filtered colimit and coherent pseudococones
statement: Let $J$ be a small filtered category and $D:J\to\mathsf{Cat}$ a strict functor with small categories as values [def-nagata-category, def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $C$ be the category formed by taking filtered colimits of the sets of objects and arrows, with the induced operations, and let $v_j:D(j)\to C$ be its structure functors [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-categories]. For any category $\mathcal A$ in the containing universe, form $\operatorname{PCone}(D,\mathcal A)$ as follows. An object consists of functors $A_j:D(j)\to\mathcal A$ and natural isomorphisms $\theta_a:A_kD(a)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_j$ for $a:j\to k$, with $\theta_1=1$ and $\theta_{ba}=\theta_a\circ(\theta_bD(a))$; an arrow to $(B_j,\eta_a)$ is a family of natural transformations $\rho_j:A_j\to B_j$ with $\rho_j\theta_a=\eta_a(\rho_kD(a))$. Restriction, with identity comparison isomorphisms, is an equivalence $\operatorname{Fun}(C,\mathcal A)\simeq\operatorname{PCone}(D,\mathcal A)$, natural in $\mathcal A$. In addition, if $K$ is small filtered and $w:K\to J$ is final, meaning each comma category $(j\downarrow w)$ is nonempty and connected, the induced functor $\varinjlim_K D(wk)\to C$ is an equivalence, compatible with the structure functors and these restriction equivalences. Objectwise equivalences between strict diagrams over $J$, equipped with coherent invertible natural comparisons along arrows, likewise induce equivalences of their filtered colimit categories compatible with their structure functors up to those comparisons.

source.place: Tag 04AX (section-directed-colimits), Tag 04E7 (lemma-cofinal), and Tag 004A (lemma-fibred-strict). The equivalence with pseudococones is the category-valued finite-representative argument extending these constructions; not attributed verbatim to one tag.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-filtered-pseudococone-effectivity] to obtain essential surjectivity of the specified restriction functor. This isolates exactly the construction of a functor from an arbitrary coherent pseudococone, not modification descent.

Prove full faithfulness directly from the supplied set-colimit universal properties. For a modification between restrictions, its compatibility square with equality comparisons says its components have equal complete arrows at objects related by a transition. Thus they define a cocone of sets with vertex Arrow(A). Mathlib CoconeTypes.IsColimit.exists_desc descends it even when A has larger universes. Object joint surjectivity identifies the descended arrow endpoints with F(X) and G(X); conjugate by these equalities. Arrow joint surjectivity reduces naturality to the stage naturality equation. The representative formula gives restriction equal to the original modification. Object joint surjectivity also shows that restriction is faithful. Postcomposition and its transformations commute with restriction definitionally, including proof irrelevance for coherence fields.
Combine the proved full faithfulness and Step 1 essential surjectivity with [lem-trf-fully-faithful-ess-surj-equivalence], using the IsEquivalence constructor, to obtain the restriction equivalence.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-functor-descent] to descend every strictly compatible functor family. Object and arrow joint surjectivity prove uniqueness of such a descent, so the given set-presented cocone is an ordinary colimit in Cat. Do this for both c and cK. Apply the colimit dual of [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-limit], directly through Mathlib Functor.Final.isColimitWhiskerEquiv, in Cat. The two colimit cocones of w composed with D have canonically isomorphic vertices. Cat.equivOfIso gives q, and the colimit comparison equations give the required strict stage-leg equations. No new category structure or separate object/arrow comparison map is constructed.

For restriction compatibility, the stage functor equations identify the functor families after precomposition by q. Both comparison isomorphisms are whiskered equality isomorphisms; equality proof irrelevance identifies them after those stage equations. A private pseudococone extensionality lemma gives equality on objects. On modifications, the components are t evaluated at q(vK_k x) and t evaluated at v_(wk)x; the stage object equation gives their heterogeneous equality. Functor.hext then proves the stated equality of restriction functors.

Finally let $E:J\to\mathsf{Cat}$ be another strict diagram, $e_j:D(j)\to E(j)$ equivalences, and $\sigma_a:E(a)e_j\xrightarrow{\sim}e_kD(a)$ coherent along identities and composition. Write $u_j:E(j)\to C_E$ for the set-colimit functors. The family $u_je_j$ has pseudococone comparisons $u_k(\sigma_a^{-1})$. Steps 1–3 produce $Q:C\to C_E$ and coherent isomorphisms $\lambda_j:Qv_j\cong u_je_j$. Every object of $C_E$ is some $u_jy$, and $y\cong e_jx$ for some $x$, proving essential surjectivity of $Q$. For fullness, move two source representatives to a common stage $j$. A morphism between their $Q$-images, conjugated by $\lambda_j$, is represented at some $a:j\to k$ by an arrow between $E(a)e_jx$ and $E(a)e_jy$. Conjugation by $\sigma_a$ changes its endpoints to $e_kD(a)x$ and $e_kD(a)y$; fullness of $e_k$ lifts it to a stage arrow of $D(k)$. Naturality and coherence of $\lambda$ show its image under $Q$ is the given morphism. For faithfulness, put two source arrows at one stage; if their $Q$-images agree, their conjugate $E$-arrows agree after a later transition by the Hom equality assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-categories]. Conjugating with $\sigma$ and using faithfulness of the later $e_k$ makes the source arrows equal there, hence equal in $C$. Thus $Q$ is an equivalence by [lem-trf-fully-faithful-ess-surj-equivalence]. The displayed $\lambda_j$, with their coherence equation, are the required compatibility with structure functors up to the given comparisons.
